Damage to several small structures in Dew and Teague.
A 69 mph gust was recorded at Richland Chambers Reservoir.
Several large trees were blown down across the county.
Quarter-size hail was reported in Lanely.
Large tree limbs were blown down.

Trees were blown down across the county.
Penny size hail fell in Fairfield.

A few large trees were split in the city of Fairfield by high winds. One tree on Cotton Street was partially leaning against a house. In addition, the underpinnings of a manufactured home on Old Palestine Road were damaged.
Freestone county sheriffs reported dime sized hail in the community of Southern Oaks.
A spotter reported quarter sized hail fell for 2 minutes near Fairfield.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Wortham.
A large tree in Fairfield was snapped by strong thunderstorm winds. Other minor tree damage was also observed in the city.
Hail stones slightly larger than the size of tennis balls fell west of Teague.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred just west of Wortham. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.8 miles and an estimated width of 100 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred approximately 4 miles southwest of Fairfield. This tornado had a path length of approximately 3.5 miles and an estimated width of 500 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75 mph.
The hail stones increased to tennis ball size in Fairfield.
